title: Discrete SIR model
prompt:
A discrete-time SIR epidemic model: a closed population of N = 39957 people; on day 0 there are 22 infected people and everyone else is susceptible. Each day the numbers are updated simultaneously from the previous day's values:
  new infections = β·S·I/N with β = 0.26,
  new recoveries = γ·I with γ = 0.08,
  S ← S − new infections, I ← I + new infections − new recoveries, R ← R + new recoveries.
Numbers are not rounded to whole people. Find S, I and R after 20 days. Give the 3 values, each with 4 significant figures, in this order, as plain decimal numbers separated by commas.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Drug concentration after repeated doses
prompt:
Pharmacokinetics, one-compartment model with instantaneous intravenous bolus doses and first-order elimination (each dose instantly raises the concentration by dose / volume; concentrations from separate doses add up). In each of the following 6 independent regimens find the requested concentration:
1. a dose of 600 mg every 12 h, 5 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 65 L, elimination half-life 14.8 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 63.1 h.
2. a dose of 90 mg every 4 h, 2 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 10 L, elimination half-life 21.7 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 34.5 h.
3. a dose of 350 mg every 6 h, 3 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 77 L, elimination half-life 24.0 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 25.5 h.
4. a dose of 320 mg every 8 h, 6 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 32 L, elimination half-life 11.0 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 12.9 h.
5. a dose of 950 mg every 6 h, 8 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 79 L, elimination half-life 23.2 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 2.8 h.
6. a dose of 760 mg every 24 h, 6 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 16 L, elimination half-life 18.8 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 62.8 h.

Give the 6 requested values, each with 4 significant figures, in the order listed, as plain decimal numbers separated by commas.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Absorbing Markov chain
prompt:
A token moves on the states S1, …, S12, W and L. Each step it moves from its current state according to the transition probabilities below (a move to the same state is allowed); W and L are absorbing (the token stays there forever).
from S1: to S3 with probability 0.3, to S5 with probability 0.3, to S12 with probability 0.2, to L with probability 0.2
from S2: to S2 with probability 0.3, to S9 with probability 0.3, to L with probability 0.4
from S3: to S1 with probability 0.3, to S3 with probability 0.2, to S4 with probability 0.1, to W with probability 0.4
from S4: to S3 with probability 0.3, to S7 with probability 0.2, to W with probability 0.5
from S5: to S5 with probability 0.4, to S12 with probability 0.3, to L with probability 0.3
from S6: to S7 with probability 0.3, to L with probability 0.7
from S7: to S11 with probability 0.1, to S12 with probability 0.3, to W with probability 0.3, to L with probability 0.3
from S8: to S4 with probability 0.3, to S9 with probability 0.6, to W with probability 0.1
from S9: to S6 with probability 0.5, to S11 with probability 0.5
from S10: to S9 with probability 0.3, to W with probability 0.4, to L with probability 0.3
from S11: to S8 with probability 0.4, to S10 with probability 0.3, to L with probability 0.3
from S12: to S4 with probability 0.7, to W with probability 0.3

The token starts in S1. Find (1) the probability that it is eventually absorbed in W and (2) the expected number of steps until it is absorbed (in W or L). Give the 2 values, each with 4 significant figures, as plain decimal numbers separated by commas.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.
